_comment: Flash and SRAM claims of this repository's patches that sit at FIXED addresses, in dm32uv-re's data/allocations.json format, plus
keep_free: ranges no Kraken build may take. Everything else Kraken uses is placed per build by tools/pack_kraken.py, which packs the
code and state into the windows minus every claim and keep_free range, and claims exactly what it used (out/.../pack/claims.json).
Plan and survey: docs/flash-allocation.md. Passed to build_manifest_patch.py with --extra-allocations by tools/build_image.py.

allocations.name: kraken_ui_data
allocations.owner: kraken_ui patch: relocated menu jump tables and label arrays (manifest data items at fixed addresses)
allocations.pinned: manifest data items (menu label arrays, jump tables) are written at fixed addresses and stock pointers are spliced to them

allocations.name: kraken_bigbuf
allocations.owner: kraken_ui .bss.big (krk_vframe.c): one 5.5 KiB buffer shared by F9 parrot and F13 burst voice (one owner at a time); F13's framing state sits in its last 0x200 bytes (link.json sram_groups)
allocations.pinned: the F9/F13 shared buffer: link.json pins F13's framing state at its tail, and the mi_rng measurement build taps it by address

allocations.name: kraken_aprs_inbox
allocations.owner: kraken_ui2/kraken_ui4 (APRS messages inbox, issue #6, F18): received APRS messages, RAM only (lost at power-off). Reached through KRK_APRS_INBOX_LO (krk_claims.h), not a linker section. Taken 2026-11-11 from the unused tail of kraken_ui_state.
allocations.pinned: reached through KRK_APRS_INBOX_LO (krk_aprs_msg.c), not by symbol

keep_free.why: kept free for the Burst Voice bench build (docs/burst-bench.md)

kept free for the bench build's state and private debug builds

_comment: Records of ours (16 bytes; the beacon text 48) inside stock data-chip logical block 4 (Radio Settings), written through stock flash_block_write.
Not flash or SRAM claims: the builder and tools/gen_claims.py read only 'allocations'. The span 0xF10-0xFEF of block 4 is reached
by no stock code, is 00 in the factory capture and in both CPS snapshots of this radio (2026-09-26) and FF in a vendor CPS write
(docs/settings-field.md 3.3); records go downwards from 0xFE0. tests/test_bvcfg.py checks the Burst Voice record against this list.
